content.inline:
# Convergent Proof of Stake

Convex peers converge on one ordering of blocks of transactions without a leader and without rounds of voting. Each peer keeps an **order** — its view of the block ordering with its consensus points — inside a signed **belief** that it gossips to the others. **Belief merge** combines the orders it receives with its own, weighted by effective stake, and adopts the winning ordering. Because every peer repeatedly adopts the majority view, orderings converge exponentially fast; consensus is the fixed point of that merge.

## Levels of confirmation

A block passes through four levels. Level 0 is the raw ordering; each higher level records the longest prefix agreed by at least **two-thirds of effective stake** at the level beneath: **proposal**, **consensus**, then **finality**. The network state is executed only against the **finalised** prefix, so "confirmed" means finalised — and finalised means executed, permanent, identical on every honest peer. There is no reorganisation, no orphaned block, no waiting for further confirmations: finality is the end of the story. Typical latency is sub-second to a few seconds.

The two-thirds thresholds give classic Byzantine tolerance: safety holds while less than a third of effective stake is adversarial.

## Stake

Peers stake CVM coins to take part; anyone may delegate stake to a peer, and delegated stake stays withdrawable by its delegator alone. **Effective** stake is not raw stake: it decays with time since the peer last produced a block, down to a small floor, so an inactive or partitioned peer loses consensus weight automatically and cannot hold the network back. Peers below a minimum effective stake cannot produce blocks at all. Peer records — key, stake, metadata — are changed only by the peer's controller account; matching a public key confers nothing.

## Two clocks

**Consensus time** is the state's timestamp, advanced only by finalised blocks; everything on-chain — scheduled transactions, memory-pool growth, stake decay, upgrade activation — keys off it, so it is the same everywhere. A peer's **wall clock** only informs its own policy. A block claims a timestamp: one more than fifteen minutes behind consensus time is invalid, and honest peers decline to finalise a future-dated block until their clocks reach it, so nobody can teleport the network forward.

## The line that keeps it honest

The state transition is a pure function of (state, block): validity and execution depend on nothing local, so any peer can replay history from genesis to a bit-identical state. Which blocks a peer proposes, which orders it adopts and when it confirms are **policy** — local choices that differ between honest peers without forking, because consensus advances only where a stake supermajority overlaps. Replay is prevented by per-account sequence numbers, checked in the transition itself.

## What this means for the owner

A transaction is final once finalised — do not wait for more. A peer sees a transaction before including it and could place its own first; that is inherent to submission, so submit through a peer you trust, whose stake is at risk under governance. Convergence, not authority, is the guarantee: no operator can reverse or exclude a finalised block.

Specifications: CAD051 (`cpos`), CAD016 (`peerstake`), CAD017 (`peerops`); the implementation's own account is `convex-core/docs/CONSENSUS.md`.
